No significant interaction was found between groups (p for interaction = 0.25). In addition, there were no patients who experienced sICH in subgroup analysis. The DAPA-TAVI trial demonstrated that dapagliflozin reduced the composite of all-cause mortality or worsening heart failure (HF) at 1 year in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with prior HF. SOURCE EXCERPT (PubMed 42983692):
Efficacy of chlorhexidine vaginal preparation in reducing postoperative infections during emergency cesarean deliveries for women in labor: a randomized controlled trial.
Postoperative infections are a leading cause of maternal morbidity after emergency cesarean delivery. This trial explores the effectiveness of preoperative vaginal cleansing via the use of chlorhexidine for reducing these complications in women in labor. This single-blinded superiority randomized controlled trial included 840 women in labor equally distributed to either immediate preoperative chlorhexidine gluconate 0.05% vaginal cleansing or no-cleansing; 826 were analyzed under a modified intention-to-treat approach. The co-primary outcomes were postcesarean endometritis and surgical site infection (SSI). Secondary outcomes included composite wound complications, postoperative fever, significant leukocytosis, hospital readmission, length of stay, and adverse drug reactions. Effects are expressed as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals, with adjusted, sensitivity, and subgroup analyses for the co-primary outcomes. Chlorhexidine significantly reduced both co-primary outcomes; postcesarean endometritis (1.9% vs. 6.3%; RR 0.303, 95% CI 0.139-0.662; P = 0.001) and SSI (1.4% vs. 5.4%; RR 0.269, 95% CI 0.110-0.656; P = 0.002); both remained significant against a Bonferroni-adjusted threshold of 0.025. Other outcomes were also reduced, including composite wound complications (3.4% vs. 11.0%; RR 0.307, 95% CI 0.171-0.550; P < 0.001), and readmission for infection (1.4% vs. 6.3%; P < 0.001; RR 0.227, 95% CI 0.095-0.547). The co-primary outcome effects persisted after adjustment and in sensitivity analyses. Treatment effects were in the same direction across premature rupture of membranes (PROM) and obesity subgroups with no significant interaction, although the SSI reduction reached significance overall and in the non-obese stratum but not within the obese stratum. In this single-center trial, preoperative chlorhexidine vaginal cleansing produced lower rates of postcesarean endometritis and SSI and of related infectious morbidity. As a low-cost intervention that can be integrated into existing perioperative workflows, it is a promising strategy for reducing maternal infection; however, adverse events were not systematically solicited, and neonatal exposure was not assessed. Multicenter confirmation, systematic maternal and neonatal safety data, and cost-effectiveness analysis are required before routine adoption. Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions (PROCEM): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Background Contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM) is increasingly used in breast cancer diagnostics; however, randomized trials assessing the added value of CEM in preoperative staging of breast cancer beyond digital mammography, digital breast tomosynthesis, and US are lacking. Purpose To assess the added value of CEM for preoperative breast cancer staging in a randomized controlled trial. Materials and Methods This prospective randomized controlled trial (Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions) enrolled women diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer eligible for primary surgery at two breast centers in Sweden. Participants were randomized 1:1 to preoperative CEM or control from November 2020 through April 2024. The primary outcome was a 10% change in treatment due to preoperative CEM findings. Secondary outcomes included differences in reoperation and mastectomy rates between groups and accuracy of malignant extent estimation with CEM, mammography/tomosynthesis, and US using histopathologic extent as the reference, assessed with Bland-Altman statistics and concordance analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed according to menopausal status, breast density, histopathologic type of cancer, lesion size, and presence of microcalcifications at baseline imaging. Results In total, 415 participants (median age, 66 years; IQR, 56-73 years) completed the trial: 202 in the CEM group and 213 in the control group. Treatment was changed in 17 of 202 participants (8.4%; 95% CI: 5.3, 13.1) based on CEM findings. No evidence of differences was observed between the CEM and control groups with regard to mastectomy (17% [35 of 202] vs 18% [39 of 213]; P = .78) or reoperation (7.9% [16 of 202] vs 10% [22 of 213]; P = .39) rates. CEM showed the closest agreement with histopathologic malignant extent (bias, 3.5 mm), outperforming mammography and/or tomosynthesis (4.8 mm) and US (10.7 mm) overall and in nine of 10 predefined subgroups, except for ductal carcinoma in situ. Conclusion This trial did not meet its primary end point of a 10% treatment change; however, preoperative CEM improved malignant extent estimation. L. reuteri supplementation also delayed SOM onset and shortened SOM duration. No significant safety concerns were observed. SOURCE EXCERPT (PubMed 42957718):
Limosilactobacillus reuteri for oral mucositis in patients undergoing radiotherapy for malignant head and neck tumors: a randomized controlled trial.
Oral mucositis (OM) is a major toxicity in patients with head and neck cancer undergoing radiotherapy. Here we conducted a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized phase II trial (NCT06285591) from March 2024 to January 2025 at West China Hospital of Sichuan University to evaluate whether Limosilactobacillus reuteri (L. reuteri) supplementation could reduce severe OM (SOM; WHO Oral Toxicity criteria grade ≥3). A total of 160 patients were randomly assigned to receive L. reuteri probiotic lozenges or placebo twice daily during radiotherapy. The primary endpoint was the incidence of SOM, and secondary endpoints included SOM onset and duration, as well as the incidence, onset, and duration of any-grade OM. Safety outcomes were monitored throughout the study. The primary endpoint was met, with a lower incidence of SOM in the L. reuteri group than in the placebo group (37.5% vs 61.3%; relative risk 0.61; 95% confidence interval 0.44-0.85; absolute risk reduction 23.8 percentage points, 95% CI 8.7% to 38.8%; P = 0.004). L. reuteri supplementation also delayed SOM onset and shortened SOM duration. No significant safety concerns were observed. These findings indicate that L. reuteri supplementation reduces SOM incidence and severity in patients with head and neck cancer receiving radiotherapy.
